title: Reading NTSTATUS values
description:
Kernel functions return an `NTSTATUS`: the top two bits are the **severity** (0 success, 1 informational, 2 warning, 3 error), bits 16-27 the facility and the low 16 bits the code. Write the helpers a driver and its user-mode client use:

```cpp
using NTSTATUS = std::int32_t;

bool ntSuccess(NTSTATUS s);                 // NT_SUCCESS: s >= 0
std::string severity(NTSTATUS s);           // "success", "informational", "warning" or "error"
std::string statusName(NTSTATUS s);         // a few well-known names, else "0x%08X"
std::uint32_t toWin32Error(NTSTATUS s);     // what GetLastError shows in user mode
```

Known names: `0x00000000` STATUS_SUCCESS, `0x00000103` STATUS_PENDING, `0x80000005` STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW, `0xC0000002` STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, `0xC000000D` STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER, `0xC0000010` STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST, `0xC0000022` STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED, `0xC0000023` STATUS_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, `0xC000009A` STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES. Unknown ones are printed as `0x` and 8 upper-case hex digits.

`toWin32Error` maps: SUCCESS → 0, PENDING → 997, BUFFER_OVERFLOW → 234, NOT_IMPLEMENTED → 1, INVALID_PARAMETER → 87, INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST → 1, ACCESS_DENIED → 5, BUFFER_TOO_SMALL → 122, INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES → 1450; anything else → 317.
hints: Shift the status as an unsigned 32-bit value: `static_cast<std::uint32_t>(s) >> 30` gives the severity directly.
lessonTitle: User Mode, Kernel Mode and Why Drivers Are Different
